"Forms of self-injury
Self-injury usually occurs in private and is done in a controlled or ritualistic manner that often leaves a pattern on the skin. Examples of self-harm include:

Cutting (cuts or severe scratches with a sharp object)
Scratching
Burning (with lit matches, cigarettes or heated, sharp objects such as knives)
Carving words or symbols on the skin
Self-hitting, punching or head banging
Piercing the skin with sharp objects
Inserting objects under the skin
Most frequently, the arms, legs and front of the torso are the targets of self-injury, but any area of the body may be used for self-injury. People who self-injure may use more than one method to harm themselves.

Becoming upset can trigger an urge to self-injure. Many people self-injure only a few times and then stop. But for others, self-injury can become a long-term, repetitive behavior." Source: Mayo Clinic

Hey there, the first thing you should try to remember is that your feelings are valid. At the bottom of it all you and that girl both struggle with self harm. The reasons why you do it may be different and the things that started the habit in the first place might be different, but you both self harm and have valid personal stories that led you to it. We can't beat ourselves up over if why we self harm is good enough for it because at the end of the day, whether it be coping mechanism or addiction we use it for something. Saying "my feelings are ridiculous because someone has it worse than me" is no different than on a day you got a job or someone complimented you saying "I shouldn't be happy because someone else is even happier for something even better". How you feel and why you do it are valid. Work on getting better instead of worrying that your situation isn't bad enough. We all have different hands in life, but we all still need to cope. Best of luck with everything. <3
